blocks.content: The Authority shall consist of a Chairperson and not more than two whole-time members and not more than two part-time members to be appointed by the Central Government.

items: Tenure of TRAI members is 3 years or 65 years of age (whichever is earlier), which is a common target for UPSC/State PSC factual questions.
Dispute resolution power lies with TDSAT, not TRAI; TRAI is primarily a regulatory and advisory body.
Members are eligible for re-appointment subject to the maximum age limit of 65 years.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI consists of a Chairperson, not more than two whole-time members, and not more than two part-time members.
The Chairperson and members are appointed directly by the Central Government of India.
The term of office for members is three years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
The 2000 amendment separated adjudicatory functions from TRAI and established the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT).
